title: ALB/NLB Access Logs and 5xx Errors

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.21 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.21 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:elb:accesslogs` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:elb:accesslogs" elb_status_code>=500
| table _time elb_status_code target_status_code request_processing_time
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.21_alb_nlb_access_logs_and_21"
| sort -_time
description: Load balancer 5xx and target failures indicate backend or LB misconfiguration. Access logs enable traffic analysis and security forensics.
value: Detecting alb/nlb access logs and 5xx errors early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable access logging for ALB/NLB to S3. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws S3 input. Collect CloudWatch metrics (RequestCount, TargetResponseTime, HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count). Alert on 5xx rate >1%.
visualization: Table (status, target, count), Line chart (5xx over time), Bar chart by target.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Web.Web
  where (Web.status >= 400 OR like(Web.status, "5%") OR like(Web.status, "403"))
  by Web.src Web.url Web.status span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Web: for HTTP/WAF/ELB access mapped to CIM `Web.Web`; confirm field names from the TA. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Known pen-test, dark-traffic, or canary 5xx during deploy; WAF in count or shadow mode you expect to list blocks for.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:elb:accesslogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `elb_status_code` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable access logging for ALB/NLB to S3. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws S3 input. Collect CloudWatch metrics (RequestCount, TargetResponseTime, HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count). Alert on 5xx rate >1%.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:elb:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:elb:accesslogs" elb_status_code>=500
| table _time elb_status_code target_status_code request_processing_time
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.21_alb_nlb_access_logs_and_21"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:elb:accesslogs` in `index=aws` to detect alb/nlb access logs and 5xx errors. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `elb_status_code` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_21_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (status, target, count), Line chart (5xx over time), Bar chart by target..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of alb/nlb access logs and 5xx errors so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
